steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Development is uneven at different scales - global (between continents and countries), national (between regions within a country), and local (between neighbourhoods). This unevenness results from a combination of physical, economic, and historical factors.

steps.title: Important
steps.body: Physical factors alone do not determine development. Countries like Singapore (hot climate, no natural resources) and Iceland (harsh climate, remote location) are HICs because they have overcome physical disadvantages through good governance, education, and strategic economic decisions.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: International migration is the movement of people from one country to another. It is a major consequence of uneven development, as people move from poorer to richer countries seeking better opportunities.

steps.title: Brain Drain
steps.body: The emigration of highly trained or qualified people from a country. For example, more Malawian doctors work in Manchester than in the whole of Malawi, severely weakening the country's healthcare system.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use named examples with specific facts and data to support your points When evaluating causes, consider physical, economic, AND historical factors - don't focus on just one For migration questions, always cover both push and pull factors Discuss both positive and negative impacts of migration for both host and source countries Use the terms LIC, NEE, and HIC rather than "developed" and "developing" For "to what extent" questions, present a balanced argument with a clear conclusion Remember: physical factors can be overcome - use counter-examples like Singapore or Iceland
